Negligence

NEG-lih-jens — contains 'neglect'; negligence is the state of neglecting your duty. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Negligence is failure to take the proper care that a situation requires.

The factory was shut down after inspectors found dangerous negligence in how chemicals were stored.

Worked Example

A daycare worker leaves toddlers unsupervised near a pool for twenty minutes while checking her phone in another room. Thankfully nothing happens, but a parent later discovers what occurred and is furious.

Failing to give proper care and attention when it was clearly required is negligence. Unlike 'mistake,' which can be a harmless slip, negligence specifically means failing in a duty to be careful.

How Negligence Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

carelessness

carelessness: a lack of proper attention or care

neglect

neglect: failure to care for or attend to something properly

oversight

oversight: a failure to notice or do something, often through carelessness

Antonyms

diligence

diligence: careful and persistent effort or attention

vigilance

vigilance: careful attention to possible danger

How Strong Is It? — carelessness → recklessness → negligence

carelessness vs. negligence

carelessness vs. negligence: Careless is a milder relative of negligent — a careless mistake is minor and often harmless, while negligence implies a real failure of duty that can cause serious harm.

recklessness vs. negligence

recklessness vs. negligence: Recklessness is stronger than negligence: negligence is a failure to take proper care, but recklessness means knowingly ignoring an obvious danger.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — neg-

prefix — neg-: not (Latin)

root — -leg-/-lig-

root — -leg-/-lig-: to pick, to choose, to gather (Latin)

suffix — -ence

suffix — -ence: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin neglegere combined neg- (not) with legere (to pick up, to attend to). Negligence is, at its root, a failure to 'pick up' or attend to something that needed care.

Use the root in a new word: eligible

Use the root in a new word: eligible: Only students with a certain grade point average are eligible to apply for the scholarship.
